title: 2027 Toyota C-HR Pricing, Specs, and Release Date
summary: The Toyota C-HR was all-new for 2026, so the 2027 model carries over unchanged. This compact, all-electric crossover has a battery range of up to 287 miles.
body_markdown:
Originally a gas-powered vehicle, the Toyota C-HR disappeared from the U.S. lineup after the 2022 model year and was re-introduced in 2026 as an all-new, all-electric compact crossover. Primary competitors for the latest version include the closely related Subaru Uncharted, the Volvo EX30, the Kia EV3, and the Hyundai Kona Electric. Although they are slightly larger, the Chevrolet Equinox EV and the Tesla Model Y could also be seen as rivals. The 2027 Toyota C-HR has two trims—SE and XSE.

## What’s New for the 2027 Toyota C-HR


The Toyota C-HR was all-new for the 2026 model year, so the 2027 model year is a direct carryover model. Toyota brought the C-HR nameplate back to the U.S. as an all-electric compact crossover that offers North American Charging Standard (NACS) ports, up to 287 miles of range, and a 14-inch infotainment screen.


## Design


The 2027 Toyota C-HR has a coupe-like profile and compact proportions. The SE trim gets 18-inch wheels, while the XSE upgrades to 20-inch wheels. While there aren’t any appearance packages, the XSE offers a black roof option that ranges from $500 to $975, depending on whether buyers pair it with a no-cost paint color or the premium Wind Chill Pearl paint.


## Powertrain


The 2027 C-HR comes standard with dual electric motors and all-wheel drive, and the combined system output is 338 horsepower. Range estimates vary based on trim, which is due to the difference in wheel sizes. The SE trim gets up to 287 miles of range, while the XSE gets up to 273 miles. Both trims come standard with NACS charging port compatibility and can charge from 10% to 80% in about 30 minutes.


## Interior


The Toyota C-HR has seatbelts for five, but four passengers will fit more comfortably. The C-HR has less rear legroom than most of its competitors, but it has competitive cargo space with 25.3 cubic feet behind the rear seats and up to 59.5 cubic feet of maximum cargo space. Standard seating surfaces are fabric and synthetic leather, and the XSE adds a light gray synthetic suede and leatherette option. A panoramic moonroof is only offered as an option ($1,000) on the XSE trim. Heated front seats and a heated steering wheel are standard, and heated rear seats are only available on the XSE as a part of the cold weather package ($450).


## Technology


The 2027 C-HR comes with a lot of standard tech features, including a 14-inch infotainment screen, wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto connectivity, two front wireless phone chargers, four USB-C ports, rain-sensing wipers, and a power liftgate. Upgrading to the XSE trim adds an eight-way power-adjustable front passenger seat, a driver’s memory seat, hands-free highway driving at low speeds, and a surround-view camera. A six-speaker audio system is standard, but a nine-speaker JBL premium audio system is available as a $600 option for the XSE trim. The C-HR also offers numerous connected services, including cloud navigation, personalized service updates, a Wi-Fi hotspot, and enhanced roadside assistance. There are free trials of varying length for each of these services, after which subscription fees apply.

## Safety


Both trims get standard Toyota Safety Sense 3.0, which includes automatic emergency braking with pedestrian detection, adaptive cruise control, lane-departure warning, lane-trace assist, and high-beam assist. Additional standard safety tech includes blind-spot monitors, rear cross-traffic alert, and safe-exit assist. Available safety features on the XSE trim include lane-change assist, hands-free traffic jam assistance for low-speed highway driving, and a surround-view camera system. Neither the Insurance Institute for Highway Safety (IIHS) nor the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration had fully crash-tested the second-gen Toyota C-HR at the time of writing, and neither had done any testing for 2027. The IIHS gave the 2026 C-HR an Acceptable score for the small overlap front test and Good ratings for the headlights and crash prevention systems.


## Pricing and Release Date


The 2027 Toyota C-HR began arriving in dealerships in September 2026. At the time of writing, Toyota listed the base price for the SE at $38,675, including a $1,595 destination fee. The XSE starts at $40,675. The SE offers a headlight cleaner for $100, as well as several accessories. The XSE has a few more options, including a cold weather package, a nine-speaker JBL premium audio system, and a panoramic moonroof. Outside of that, there is one premium paint color, Wind Chill Pearl, for $475.
